findings.issue_text: [BUG] <%= raw post.cooked %> renders fully unsanitized HTML, because the new raw_html cook_method makes Post#cook return the raw RSS/imported content verbatim with no sanitizer in the pipeline. Any malicious HTML/JavaScript in a polled RSS feed item or in a remote page fetched via TopicEmbed.import_remote is served unescaped to every anonymous visitor of the embed endpoint, giving the feed/origin author stored XSS against the Discourse origin and the embedding site.

[BUG] The embed stylesheet is referenced via stylesheet_link_tag 'embed' but 'embed' is never added to config.assets.precompile (the diff touches no initializer/application.rb), so in production Sprockets has no precompiled 'embed' CSS asset. On any production deploy the /embed/best route renders with no stylesheet (404 on /assets/embed.css), breaking the feature for all embedding sites until an operator manually adds the asset to the precompile list.

[ADVISORY] embed.js executes an IIFE that immediately reads document.getElementById('discourse-comments') and the globals discourseUrl/discourseEmbedUrl, but this diff ships no snippet, docs, or template that defines those globals, and the file is not referenced by any view or asset manifest. The embed script is inert as shipped: third-party site operators have no supported way to obtain a snippet that sets discourseUrl/discourseEmbedUrl before the script runs, and if the file is ever pulled into the application.js bundle it throws TypeError on null comments, breaking every page's JS.

[ADVISORY] The diff adds force: true to create_table :top_topics, which silently DROPs any existing top_topics table (and its data) before recreating it. Any environment that already ran the original migration and now runs the modified version loses all TopTopic rows — daily/weekly/monthly period aggregates — with no warning; force: true belongs in schema.rb dumps, not in a migration applied to live databases.

[ADVISORY] The new embed stylesheet //= requires ./vendor/normalize and ./common/foundation/base, pulling the full foundation/base SCSS variables into a stylesheet intended for a cross-origin iframe on third-party sites. If foundation/base later grows dependencies (images, fonts, further requires), the embed CSS silently inherits them, inflating payload and creating compile breakage on the embed route whenever those partials change — a hidden coupling between the embed stylesheet and the app's core SCSS with no test covering its compilation.

[ADVISORY] The new admin category label 'embedding' in client.en.yml is dead code: this diff adds no client-side admin UI (no settings route, no template) that references the admin.categories.embedding key, and none of the four new site settings are marked client: true. The label ships with no consumer, so the embedding settings it names cannot be edited from the admin UI — an operator must set embeddable_host, feed_polling_enabled, feed_polling_url and embed_by_username from the console/rake, otherwise /embed/best returns 403 for every request.

[ADVISORY] poll_feed calls i.content.scrub unconditionally, but SimpleRSS items from plain RSS 2.0 feeds expose description, not content, so i.content is nil for feeds lacking an atom:content element. The hourly scheduled job crashes with NoMethodError (nil.scrub) on the first description-only RSS item; with retry: false set in sidekiq_options the poll silently dies and no feed items are ever imported, and the exception recurs every hour.

[BUG] The resize postMessage targets request.referer, which breaks after the loading page's 30-second self-reload makes the iframe's referer the embed/best URL itself instead of the embedding page. When /embed/best initially finds no topic, the loading view reloads itself after 30s (embed/loading.html.erb line 10); on that reload the browser sets the referer to the iframe's own /embed/best URL, so parent.postMessage(..., '/embed/best URL') fails the origin check in embed.js (discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1) and the parent never receives 'discourse-resize' — the iframe stays at its initial height and the embedded comments render clipped or with a huge empty box on every page that went through the loading path.

[BUG] poll_feed calls SimpleRSS.parse open(...) with no rescue around any of the network/parsing calls, and sidekiq_options retry: false guarantees the failure is permanent. Any transient network error, 5xx, or malformed feed byte while opening feed_polling_url raises inside the scheduled job; because retry is disabled the exception kills the run, the remaining feed items in that hour are never imported, and the admin gets no signal — feed imports silently stop until someone inspects sidekiq dead sets manually.

[BUG] poll_feed passes i.title straight into TopicEmbed.import, and import creates the topic with skip_validations: true, so a feed item with a nil or blank title produces a topic with a nil title. Atom/RSS entries legitimately omit <title>; TopicEmbed.import builds PostCreator.new(user, title: nil, ..., skip_validations: true), creating a Topic whose title is nil. Every later render of that topic (topic list, embed/best view calling @topic_view.topic.url which builds a slug from the title) hits nil-derived slugs or list-layout breakage, and there is no code path in this diff that rejects or defaults a blank feed title.

[BUG] feed_key (the feed-modified cache) is defined but never called, so the polling job re-processes every feed item on every hourly run with no Last-Modified/ETag check anywhere in the diff. The cache key infrastructure that was evidently intended to gate polling exists as dead code; every hour the full feed is re-fetched and every item runs through TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: ...).first plus a SHA1 comparison. On a large feed this is an unbounded per-hour DB scan that grows with feed size, and the dead method misleads the next maintainer into believing caching exists.

[ADVISORY] embed.js reads the globals discourseUrl and discourseEmbedUrl with no guard, and the iframe is created with no initial height, so any embedding page that fails to define both globals exactly gets a broken or invisible comment box. A publisher who copies the JS but names the variable discourseURL or sets it after the script runs gets an immediate ReferenceError and no comments render at all; even on the happy path the iframe has no height until the first postMessage arrives, so pages flash a zero-height box or clip content when the resize message is lost (e.g. the reload-referer case above).

[ADVISORY] The loading view unconditionally reloads every 30 seconds with no retry limit and no terminal failure state, while every retrieval path in TopicRetriever can silently no-op (embed_by_username user missing, readability failure, invalid host). When retrieval permanently fails — e.g. embed_by_username names a deleted user so fetch_http returns nil, or Readability raises inside the job — the embedded page enters an infinite reload loop, hammering /embed/best from every visitor's browser every 30 seconds and enqueuing a throttled RetrieveTopic job each minute per URL, with the end reader seeing 'Loading Discussion...' forever and the admin getting no error surfaced anywhere.

[ADVISORY] The new non-trivial retrieval logic — TopicRetriever#perform_retrieve, its Redis throttle, the re-check after PollFeed, fetch_http's user lookup, TopicEmbed.import_remote readability extraction, and the entire Jobs::RetrieveTopic job — has no test anywhere in the diff. Every spec in this file stubs perform_retrieve or its callers; a regression in perform_retrieve (e.g. the $redis.setnx/expire throttle leaking a key with no TTL on exception, or the exists?-check ordering) ships undetected, and TopicEmbed.import_remote — which fetches and parses arbitrary remote HTML into stored raw content — has zero verification of what tags/attributes survive the Readability whitelist.

[ADVISORY] The best action builds TopicView.new(topic_id, current_user, {best: 5}) with no handling of the topic having been deleted, closed, or unlisted since the TopicEmbed row was created. An admin who deletes a topic (or its forum category becomes restricted) leaves a dangling TopicEmbed row; the next embed load constructs a TopicView for a deleted/inaccessible topic, producing a 500 or a permission error rendered inside the embedding site's iframe instead of falling back to the 'start discussion' state the loading/best views otherwise handle.

[BUG] Adding `force: true` to the pre-existing create_top_topics migration makes it drop and recreate the top_topics table on any install that has already run it. Operators who already applied this migration (the table exists) will have all top_topics rows destroyed and recreated empty on the next schema operation; permanent loss of top-topic aggregate data, and it has nothing to do with the embedding feature.

[ADVISORY] The Disqus import task silently drops the `--category` option and the original `created_at` timestamps, rerouting through TopicEmbed.import_remote instead of PostCreator — a behavior change to an existing tool that is not traceable to the embedding requirement. Anyone running the documented `disqus import -c <category>` invocation now gets a hard Thor error (unknown option) with no replacement, and imported posts lose their original creation dates; the user is bitten on the next import run.

[BUG] `i.content.scrub` crashes with NoMethodError when a feed item has no content element (common for RSS 2.0 feeds or Atom entries with only a summary). The hourly PollFeed job raises mid-loop, aborting import of all remaining items; with retry: false the whole feed import silently stops at the first malformed item until manual intervention.

[ADVISORY] The raw_html cook path returns `raw` before `Plugin::Filter.apply(:after_post_cook, ...)`, so plugins registered on that filter are silently bypassed for imported posts — a core pipeline behavioral fork introduced solely to serve embedding. Site operators relying on plugins that hook after_post_cook (e.g. link rewriting, media transformations) get inconsistent behavior: every RSS-imported post skips those transforms with no setting to control it.

[ADVISORY] The resize postMessage is sent to `request.referer` as targetOrigin, coupling the embed layout to a header that is only guaranteed present because of the controller filter — and embed.js checks `discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin)` with no trailing-slash handling on either side. Any deployment where SiteSetting base_url has a trailing slash or the browser suppresses Referer (privacy settings, meta referrer) breaks iframe auto-resize, leaving the embed iframe stuck at default height; users see clipped comments.

[ADVISORY] `response.headers['X-Frame-Options'] = "ALLOWALL"` is placed after the raising referer check and inside a method whose rescue re-raises, so the header-setting line is dead code on every rejection path. Maintainers reading the filter conclude the header is always applied; the successful path works only by accident of ordering, and any refactor that reorders the lines will silently drop the clickjacking relaxation the embed depends on.

[BUG] PollFeed crashes with NoMethodError when a feed item has no content element (plain RSS 2.0 feeds expose description, not content/content:encoded), because i.content is nil and nil.scrub raises. Any RSS (non-Atom) feed whose items lack content:encoded kills the entire poll job on the first item; every subsequent item in that feed is never imported and the scheduled job fails hourly with no partial progress.

[BUG] TopicEmbed.import's update path does `post = embed.post; PostRevisor.new(post)` with no nil check, so an embed whose post was deleted crashes, and since import is called in a loop over all feed items, one bad embed aborts the whole poll. A single topic/post deleted by a moderator (posts can be deleted while topic_embeds rows persist — there is no dependent destroy or FK) makes Jobs::PollFeed raise mid-loop, permanently poisoning all feed imports for every item after that one.

[BUG] The loading view reloads unconditionally every 30 seconds forever, even when the RetrieveTopic job can never succeed (e.g. embed_by_username unset so fetch_http returns early, or the embed_url host check fails after enqueue). Every visitor to a page whose article can never be imported drives an infinite reload loop in their browser, each cycle hitting /embed/best and enqueueing another RetrieveTopic job (throttled only per-URL for 60s), producing permanent background job churn and a never-loading embed.

[ADVISORY] feed_key computes a SHA1-based 'feed-modified' cache key but nothing in the diff ever reads or writes it, so the intended conditional-fetch/last-poll dedupe was never wired up. Every hourly poll re-opens and fully parses the feed and runs TopicEmbed.where(embed_url:).first plus a SHA1 comparison for every historical item — a 5-year blog with thousands of items does thousands of pointless DB lookups per poll forever, and the dead method misleads the next maintainer into thinking caching exists.

[ADVISORY] perform_retrieve synchronously invokes Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({}) inline — a full-site feed fetch, parse, and per-item import — inside the single-URL retrieve job, coupling one embed request to the entire feed pipeline. A visitor embedding one new article blocks a Sidekiq worker for the duration of downloading and importing the whole feed; with the no_throttle staff bypass, concurrent embed views each trigger full feed polls, multiplying load and serializing behind a single global feed_polling_url setting that the data model can't extend to multiple feeds.

[ADVISORY] The raw_html cook_method early-returns before Plugin::Filter.apply(:after_post_cook, ...), so one category of posts silently bypasses the plugin cooking contract that all other posts pass through. Any site relying on an after_post_cook plugin filter (e.g. Onebox rewriting, link normalization, profanity filtering) gets none of it on imported feed posts, and a plugin author debugging 'works for user posts but not imported posts' has no indication the branch was skipped.

[ADVISORY] topic_id and post_id are plain integer columns with no foreign keys or indexes, so nothing prevents a topic_embed row pointing at a deleted/nonexistent topic or post, and topic-side lookups (given a topic, find its embed) require a full scan. Deleting a topic or post leaves an orphaned topic_embeds row; the next import for that URL takes the update path and crashes (see separate finding), and any future admin query 'which embed belongs to topic X' has no index to use.

[BUG] The disqus import thor task silently drops the documented `:category` / `-c` option, so all imported topics now land in uncategorized regardless of the operator's command line. Operators running `thor disqus:import -c mycategory` after this deploy get every imported thread in the wrong (uncategorized) category with no error — the option is simply ignored; the diff gives no human-accepted rationale for removing the capability.

[BUG] An already-shipped, unrelated migration (`CreateTopTopics`) is edited in this PR to add `force: true`, which drops and recreates the table on databases that already ran it or rebuild from scratch mid-PR. Any environment where this migration runs again (db:reset-adjacent workflows, fresh clones interleaved with the change) silently destroys top_topics data; this is scope creep into an unrelated migration with no accepted justification in the PR's stated intent.

[ADVISORY] The `raw_html` cook path returns `raw` before `Plugin::Filter.apply(:after_post_cook, ...)` runs, so posts imported via embeds silently bypass every registered after_post_cook plugin hook. Sites relying on plugins that mutate cooked output (onebox rewriting, affiliate stripping, custom sanitization) get unsanitized, unfiltered HTML in embed-imported posts rendered with `raw post.cooked` in embed views; plugin authors and admins have no signal that the hook contract no longer holds for these posts.

[ADVISORY] The revisor's save behavior is globally changed from unconditional `@post.save` to `@post.save(validate: !@opts[:skip_validations])`, altering the validation contract for every existing caller of revise!, not just the embed importer that needed it. Any existing code path that calls revise! with user-controlled opts can now persist invalid posts whenever skip_validations leaks in, and future revisor callers inherit an easy validation-bypass footgun — a core-object semantic change hidden inside a feature PR about embedding.

[BUG] TopicEmbed.import stores externally-fetched content as raw HTML with no sanitization, and the embed view renders it with `raw post.cooked`, enabling stored XSS. The feed-polling path passes CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content) straight into PostCreator with cook_method raw_html, which makes Post#cook return the raw string verbatim (app/models/post.rb `return raw if cook_method == Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`), and app/views/embed/best.html.erb renders `<%= raw post.cooked %>` — so any <script>, inline event handler, or javascript: link in the RSS/Atom item content executes in every visitor's browser on the embedding site. If the polled feed (or a MITM on the plain-http feed URL) is compromised, the attacker runs script in the Discourse origin and the embeddable host.

[BUG] The imported-from footer interpolates the URL directly into an HTML attribute without escaping: `contents << "
#{I18n.t('embed.imported_from', link: "#{url}")} "`. The only URL validation is the prefix regex /^https?:///, so an embed_url or RSS item link like `http://eviltrout.com/x' onmouseover=alert(1) b='` (host matches embeddable_host, satisfying TopicRetriever#invalid_host?) breaks out of the href attribute; since the post is cooked as raw_html and rendered with `raw`, this is stored XSS in the Discourse embed page triggered by any user who requests /embed/best with that embed_url.

[BUG] The postMessage origin check uses substring containment (`discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1`) instead of exact origin equality, so any origin whose string contains the Discourse URL passes. A malicious page at https://eviltrout.com.attacker.com (or any URL embedding the discourse base URL as a substring) passes the check and can drive the iframe via cross-origin messages; currently the only effect is setting iframe height, but the guard is a broken security boundary that later message types will inherit.

[ADVISORY] The SSRF host check (invalid_host?) is enforced once before the fetch, but open-uri transparently follows HTTP redirects, so the embeddable_host check does not constrain where the actual request lands. The embeddable host (or anything that can make it issue a 302) can redirect open(url) to http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/ or an internal service; the retrieved body is then run through Readability and stored/rendered as raw HTML, letting the operator of the configured host exfiltrate internal-network responses through the Discourse embed.

[ADVISORY] ensure_embeddable gates the endpoint on the Referer header, which is client-controlled and trivially spoofed by any non-browser or headless client, so the referer-host check provides no real access control. Any attacker can curl /embed/best?embed_url=... with a forged Referer to bypass the host gate; impact is currently limited to triggering RetrieveTopic jobs (throttled to once/60s per URL per non-staff user) and viewing public topic content, but the control is security theater and downstream code treats it as an authorization decision.

[BUG] The three guard tests are tautological: each stubs only one SiteSetting while the other two already default to disabled/blank, so every test passes even if the corresponding guard in Jobs::PollFeed#execute is deleted. Deleting `SiteSetting.feed_polling_enabled? &&` (or either other condition) from execute leaves the suite green; the guard logic that prevents the job from polling an unconfigured feed is verified by nothing. The author's counter-argument is 'stubs isolate each condition' — but they don't: the unstubbed settings' defaults already make poll_feed unreachable, so the tests never discriminate a present guard from an absent one.

[BUG] The first two tests assert only `response.should_not be_success`, which is satisfied by any failure mode, including the before_filter's Discourse::InvalidAccess from the blank default embeddable_host rather than the param-missing / host-missing behavior they claim to test. The 'is 404 without an embed_url' test would pass identically if `params.require(:embed_url)` were removed and the action returned 200 with a nil embed_url — the actual contract (400/404 for missing param vs 403 for host errors) is never distinguished, so a regression to a wrong status code or wrong error path ships undetected.

[BUG] The success-context tests exercise only mocks: `TopicView.expects(:new)` returns nil (so the template renders against a nil @topic_view), `TopicRetriever.expects` replaces the retrieval, and the only real-behavior assertion lives in a shared `after` block, so neither test verifies rendered output, the enqueued job's arguments (user_id, embed_url), or the render of 'loading'. If EmbedController#best stopped enqueuing :retrieve_topic with the right embed_url, or rendered the wrong template, or TopicView were constructed with wrong options, these tests still pass as long as a mock was poked; the mocha stub for TopicView.new returning nil means the view layer is never genuinely exercised and any template crash is masked by the assertion-free it-block body.

[BUG] The 'valid host' tests stub `retrieved_recently?` and mock `perform_retrieve`, so TopicRetriever's actual Redis throttle ($redis.setnx/expire 60s) and perform_retrieve's dedup/feed-polling/fetch_http branches are never executed by any test in the diff. A broken retrieved_recently? (e.g. setnx key typo, missing expire leaking keys forever, or the throttle never firing so every embed request re-fetches the remote site) passes this suite unchanged; the tests only verify that a mocked method is called when another mocked method returns false — a tautology against the real code.

[ADVISORY] The 'Supports updating the post' test checks only that the new content appears, never that exactly one TopicEmbed/topic still exists (no duplicate topic created on re-import) nor that content_sha1 was updated. The update path's main risk — re-import creating a second topic because the embed lookup or content_sha1 comparison regressed — would still satisfy the regex assertion; a future change breaking the `embed.blank?` branch silently doubles topics per feed poll, and this spec stays green.

[ADVISORY] The only positive test asserts `poll_feed` is invoked once and nothing else, so PollFeed#poll_feed's entire body — feed parsing, `i.link`/`i.id` fallback, CGI.unescapeHTML, content scrub, and the TopicEmbed.import call per item — has zero coverage in this diff. A crash in poll_feed (e.g. `i.content` nil raising on .scrub, or open() raising on a bad feed URL) reaches production the first time an admin enables feed polling, because every spec stops at the delegation boundary; with `retry: false` in sidekiq_options the job fails permanently with no diagnostics.

[ADVISORY] No test in the diff exercises TopicRetriever#perform_retrieve, #fetch_http, or TopicEmbed.import_remote, and no spec file references them (checked spec/components/topic_retriever_spec.rb, spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb, spec/models/topic_embed_spec.rb, spec/jobs/poll_feed_spec.rb — all mock or bypass these methods). The invalid_host? rescue-branch ordering, the feed_polling shortcut, and the embed_by_username user lookup in fetch_http are the live code paths serving every embed request, yet a typo in any of them ships undetected; the retriever spec's guard tests pass against a TopicRetriever whose retrieve body is `nil`.

[BUG] force: true is added to the already-shipped CreateTopTopics migration, making it destructive on re-run. Any environment that re-runs this migration (db:migrate:redo, restored schema_migrations, or a re-cloned setup importing a dump with the table populated) silently DROPs the existing top_topics table and destroys all its data before recreating it empty; the lens's exact 'shipped migration made destructive on re-run' failure.

[BUG] create_table :topic_embeds uses force: true, so any pre-existing topic_embeds table (e.g. left by a failed first run or a parallel deploy) is silently dropped with all its embed mappings. An operator re-running the migration after a partial/failed application loses the topic_id/post_id/embed_url associations, orphaning imported topics from their source URLs and causing duplicate topics on the next feed poll.

[ADVISORY] The Disqus import path switched from PostCreator with created_at: Date.parse(t[:created_at]) to TopicEmbed.import_remote, which drops the original creation date entirely. Anyone importing a Disqus export after this change gets topics dated 'now' instead of their historical dates — a field-fidelity loss on migration data; the created_at plumbing exists in PostCreator but is never passed by the new code path.

[ADVISORY] TopicEmbed.import update path uses PostRevisor#revise! but never updates the topic title when the feed title changes, and a revisor failure leaves content_sha1 unchanged only because update_column runs after — but if revise! raises (invalid content), the rescue is absent and the scheduled job (retry: false) permanently skips that item. Feed items whose revision raises lose their update forever (PollFeed has sidekiq_options retry: false, so the exception kills the entire poll run mid-list and subsequent items are never processed until the next hour's partial re-run hits the same item again).

[BUG] The rss.items loop has no per-item or per-feed error handling, so a single malformed item aborts the entire poll mid-loop with no log and no error surfaced. If any item's i.content is nil (valid in RSS/Atom) `i.content.scrub` raises NoMethodError, or if any item's link/id resolution fails, the job dies after importing a prefix of the feed: the remaining items are silently skipped while the already-imported ones look successful, and sidekiq_options retry: false means nothing retries or reports until the next hourly run, which fails the same way — a persistent silent partial import.

[BUG] SimpleRSS.parse open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url) performs an outbound HTTP fetch with no timeout. A slow or hung feed host blocks the Sidekiq worker thread indefinitely; with retry: false the poll is not retried, and because TopicRetriever#perform_retrieve invokes this same poll synchronously inside a RetrieveTopic job, one hung feed also wedges the embed-retrieval job and the user's iframe stays on the loading page with no timeout ever firing.

[BUG] TopicEmbed.import_remote calls open(url).read with no timeout and no size cap on the download. A request to /embed/best for a page whose host accepts the connection but stalls leaves the RetrieveTopic worker blocked forever on a socket read; the controller meanwhile rendered 'loading' and reported success (200), so the embed is never created and the end user reloads into the same loop indefinitely.

[BUG] The update path assumes embed.post is non-nil, but TopicEmbed has no dependency on the post surviving; PostRevisor.new(post).revise! crashes when the referenced post was deleted. When a feed re-import hits an embed whose post was deleted (post_id null: false does not prevent the post row itself being removed), PostRevisor.new(nil) raises NoMethodError inside the scheduled poll, aborting the remaining feed items with no recovery and no log of which URL was at fault.

[BUG] TopicView.new(topic_id, ...) raises when the topic_embed row points at a deleted or otherwise unviewable topic, producing a raw 500 in the embed iframe. Once an embed's topic is deleted (or made restricted for anonymous viewers), every /embed/best request for that URL returns a 500 error page inside the publisher's iframe instead of a 4xx or the loading/fallback view, permanently breaking comments on that article.

[ADVISORY] The retrieve is fire-and-forget: the controller enqueues RetrieveTopic and renders 'loading' with no path for the job's failure to ever reach the user. If the retrieval job fails (unreachable article, readability returning no content, or the throttle/redis path erroring), the iframe reloads every 30 seconds forever showing 'Loading Discussion...' — the site owner gets no error signal, and each reload enqueues another job that silently no-ops, so the failure is invisible on both the user page and Discourse's own UI.

[ADVISORY] perform_retrieve invokes the full hourly feed poll (Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})) synchronously and inline inside the RetrieveTopic job. Every embed miss pays the cost of fetching and re-importing the entire RSS feed inline — combined with the missing timeout above, a large or slow feed multiplies worker occupancy, and the scheduled hourly poll plus these inline polls can run concurrently against the same feed with no lock, double-importing or racing on TopicEmbed.create! (unique index then raises ActiveRecord::RecordNotUnique aborting the job).

[ADVISORY] feed_key (the 'feed-modified:<sha1>' cache key) is computed but never read or written — the conditional-fetch caching it implies was never wired up. Every hourly poll and every inline poll from TopicRetriever fully re-downloads and re-processes the entire feed regardless of whether it changed; a large feed costs full bandwidth and full TopicEmbed.import reconciliation work each cycle, and the dead key misleads the next maintainer into believing modification-checking exists.

[ADVISORY] TopicEmbed.import imposes no cap on the number of feed items processed or the size of content stored, and the feed loop iterates every item unconditionally. A feed (or an attacker-controlled embedded page, given the referer check only validates host) can supply arbitrarily many items or arbitrarily large article bodies, which are stored verbatim as raw_html posts — unbounded DB growth and job runtime per poll with no maximum to stop it.

goldens.comment: The PollFeed job calls open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url) without validating the URL, allowing an attacker who controls the feed_polling_url site setting to make the server fetch arbitrary internal or external URLs.
The current origin validation using indexOf is insufficient and can be bypassed. An attacker could use a malicious domain like evil-discourseUrl.com to pass this check.
postMessage targetOrigin should be the origin (scheme+host+port), not the full referrer URL; using the full URL will cause the message to be dropped and prevent resizing.

The code sets X-Frame-Options: ALLOWALL which completely disables clickjacking protection. The referer validation can be bypassed (referer headers are easily spoofed), and the fallback to empty string for nil referer masks validation failures.

The TopicEmbed.import method is susceptible to a NoMethodError if the contents parameter is nil when attempting to append a string, and an XSS vulnerability due to unescaped url interpolation in the generated HTML.
The ERB block closes with end if, which is invalid Ruby/ERB and will raise at render; it should just be end to close the if block.

Calling `i.content.scrub` assumes that `i.content` is always populated. However, many RSS feeds do not provide a `content` field, leading to a potential nil pointer exception when `i.content` is nil. A fallback to `description` should be implemented to prevent crashes.

An unescaped request header (request.referer) is interpolated into JavaScript without proper escaping, which can lead to XSS vulnerabilities if the referer contains malicious content. This issue can allow attackers to execute arbitrary scripts in the context of the application.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] <%= raw post.cooked %> renders fully unsanitized HTML, because the new raw_html cook_method makes Post#cook return the raw RSS/imported content verbatim with no sanitizer in the pipeline. Any malicious HTML/JavaScript in a polled RSS feed item or in a remote page fetched via TopicEmbed.import_remote is served unescaped to every anonymous visitor of the embed endpoint, giving the feed/origin author stored XSS against the Discourse origin and the embedding site.

adjudication.rationale: The diff explicitly adds a `:raw_html` cook method where `Post#cook` returns `raw` verbatim (`return raw if cook_method == Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`), bypassing the normal cooking/sanitization pipeline. `TopicEmbed.import` creates posts with `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` and supplies `raw` directly from RSS (`SimpleRSS.parse ... i.content`) or remote readability output (`doc.content`) without any sanitizer in this diff. The embed view then renders posts with `<%= raw post.cooked %>`, so for `raw_html` posts `post.cooked == post.raw` and any malicious HTML/JS in feed content would be served unescaped from the embed endpoint.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The diff adds force: true to create_table :top_topics, which silently DROPs any existing top_topics table (and its data) before recreating it. adjudication.rationale: The diff does change `db/migrate/20131223171005_create_top_topics.rb` from `create_table :top_topics do |t|` to `create_table :top_topics, force: true do |t|`. adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] poll_feed calls SimpleRSS.parse open(...) with no rescue around any of the network/parsing calls, and sidekiq_options retry: false guarantees the failure is permanent. Any transient network error, 5xx, or malformed feed byte while opening feed_polling_url raises inside the scheduled job; because retry is disabled the exception kills the run, the remaining feed items in that hour are never imported, and the admin gets no signal — feed imports silently stop until someone inspects sidekiq dead sets manually.

adjudication.rationale: In `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb`, `poll_feed` does `SimpleRSS.parse open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` with no error handling, and the job is configured with `sidekiq_options retry: false`. adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] poll_feed passes i.title straight into TopicEmbed.import, and import creates the topic with skip_validations: true, so a feed item with a nil or blank title produces a topic with a nil title. Atom/RSS entries legitimately omit <title>; TopicEmbed.import builds PostCreator.new(user, title: nil, ..., skip_validations: true), creating a Topic whose title is nil. Every later render of that topic (topic list, embed/best view calling @topic_view.topic.url which builds a slug from the title) hits nil-derived slugs or list-layout breakage, and there is no code path in this diff that rejects or defaults a blank feed title.

adjudication.rationale: In `Jobs::PollFeed#poll_feed`, each feed item calls `TopicEmbed.import(user, url, i.title, content)` without checking for a blank/nil `i.title`. In `TopicEmbed.import`, a new topic/post is created via `PostCreator.new(..., title: title, ..., skip_validations: true, ...)`, and this diff adds no guard/default for an empty title. While the diff doesn’t prove the DB/`PostCreator` will actually allow a nil title (it may error on constraints/other validations), it does show an unhandled legitimate feed edge case that could lead to invalid records or failed imports.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] feed_key (the feed-modified cache) is defined but never called, so the polling job re-processes every feed item on every hourly run with no Last-Modified/ETag check anywhere in the diff. The cache key infrastructure that was evidently intended to gate polling exists as dead code; every hour the full feed is re-fetched and every item runs through TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: ...).first plus a SHA1 comparison. On a large feed this is an unbounded per-hour DB scan that grows with feed size, and the dead method misleads the next maintainer into believing caching exists.

adjudication.rationale: In `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb`, `feed_key` is defined (lines creating `"feed-modified:#{Digest::SHA1...}"`) but never referenced anywhere in the diff. `poll_feed` always does `SimpleRSS.parse open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` and iterates `rss.items.each`, calling `TopicEmbed.import(...)` for every item on every run, with no use of Last-Modified/ETag or any Redis/cache gating. While `TopicEmbed.import` avoids duplicating by URL and SHA1, it still performs a per-item DB lookup (`TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: url).first`) each hour, making this a real performance/maintainability concern and the unused method is misleading, but it’s not a correctness-breaking defect by itself.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] embed.js reads the globals discourseUrl and discourseEmbedUrl with no guard, and the iframe is created with no initial height, so any embedding page that fails to define both globals exactly gets a broken or invisible comment box. A publisher who copies the JS but names the variable discourseURL or sets it after the script runs gets an immediate ReferenceError and no comments render at all; even on the happy path the iframe has no height until the first postMessage arrives, so pages flash a zero-height box or clip content when the resize message is lost (e.g. the reload-referer case above).

adjudication.rationale: In the new app/assets/javascripts/embed.js, the code directly references the undeclared globals `discourseUrl` and `discourseEmbedUrl` when setting `iframe.src` (`iframe.src = discourseUrl + ... encodeURIComponent(discourseEmbedUrl);`). If either global is missing or defined after this script executes, the script will throw a ReferenceError and the embed will fail. Also, the iframe’s height is never initialized (only set upon receiving a `discourse-resize` postMessage), so if the resize message never arrives the iframe may remain at an incorrect default height and clip content.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The loading view unconditionally reloads every 30 seconds with no retry limit and no terminal failure state, while every retrieval path in TopicRetriever can silently no-op (embed_by_username user missing, readability failure, invalid host). When retrieval permanently fails — e.g. embed_by_username names a deleted user so fetch_http returns nil, or Readability raises inside the job — the embedded page enters an infinite reload loop, hammering /embed/best from every visitor's browser every 30 seconds and enqueuing a throttled RetrieveTopic job each minute per URL, with the end reader seeing 'Loading Discussion...' forever and the admin getting no error surfaced anywhere.

adjudication.rationale: The new loading view reloads unconditionally every 30s (`app/views/embed/loading.html.erb` uses `setTimeout(document.location.reload(), 30000)` with no limit). In `EmbedController#best`, when `TopicEmbed.topic_id_for_embed` returns nil it always enqueues `Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, ..., embed_url: embed_url)` and renders `loading`. Several retrieval paths shown can permanently no-op without surfacing an error (e.g., `TopicRetriever#fetch_http` returns early if `embed_by_username` user is missing; `TopicEmbed.import_remote` calls `open(url).read` and `Readability::Document.new` with no rescue). In such cases the embed never becomes available, so the iframe page will reload forever and keep hitting `/embed/best` and enqueueing `retrieve_topic` jobs repeatedly (even if the actual fetch is throttled inside `TopicRetriever#retrieved_recently?`).

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The new non-trivial retrieval logic — TopicRetriever#perform_retrieve, its Redis throttle, the re-check after PollFeed, fetch_http's user lookup, TopicEmbed.import_remote readability extraction, and the entire Jobs::RetrieveTopic job — has no test anywhere in the diff. Every spec in this file stubs perform_retrieve or its callers; a regression in perform_retrieve (e.g. the $redis.setnx/expire throttle leaking a key with no TTL on exception, or the exists?-check ordering) ships undetected, and TopicEmbed.import_remote — which fetches and parses arbitrary remote HTML into stored raw content — has zero verification of what tags/attributes survive the Readability whitelist.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds substantial new behavior in `TopicRetriever#perform_retrieve` (redis throttle via `setnx`/`expire`, `TopicEmbed.exists?` re-checks, optional PollFeed invocation, and `fetch_http` user lookup), `Jobs::RetrieveTopic#execute`, and `TopicEmbed.import_remote` (remote `open(url).read` + `Readability::Document` whitelist). The added specs do not cover these paths: `spec/components/topic_retriever_spec.rb` stubs `retrieved_recently?` and only asserts whether `perform_retrieve` is invoked, `spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb` mocks the retriever and never exercises retrieval logic, `spec/jobs/poll_feed_spec.rb` only tests `execute` gating not `poll_feed` parsing/open, and `spec/models/topic_embed_spec.rb` tests `.import` but not `.import_remote`. So regressions inside `perform_retrieve`/throttling and the remote HTML extraction/whitelisting would indeed be untested in this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The best action builds TopicView.new(topic_id, current_user, {best: 5}) with no handling of the topic having been deleted, closed, or unlisted since the TopicEmbed row was created. An admin who deletes a topic (or its forum category becomes restricted) leaves a dangling TopicEmbed row; the next embed load constructs a TopicView for a deleted/inaccessible topic, producing a 500 or a permission error rendered inside the embedding site's iframe instead of falling back to the 'start discussion' state the loading/best views otherwise handle.

adjudication.rationale: In `EmbedController#best`, the presence of a `topic_id` from `TopicEmbed.topic_id_for_embed(embed_url)` unconditionally leads to `TopicView.new(topic_id, current_user, {best: 5})` with no guard that the topic still exists or is viewable. Since `topic_embeds` has only an `embed_url` unique index and no shown cascading cleanup, a deleted topic could leave a dangling `TopicEmbed` row (per the migration/model), and the controller has no fallback path (it only falls back when `topic_id` is nil). The diff does not show how `TopicView.new` behaves on missing/inaccessible topics, so the exact 500/permission rendering outcome can’t be proven from the diff, but the missing edge-case handling is real and diff-grounded.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] Adding `force: true` to the pre-existing create_top_topics migration makes it drop and recreate the top_topics table on any install that has already run it. Operators who already applied this migration (the table exists) will have all top_topics rows destroyed and recreated empty on the next schema operation; permanent loss of top-topic aggregate data, and it has nothing to do with the embedding feature.

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes an *old* migration to `create_table :top_topics, force: true`. In Rails, migrations are not re-run on an existing install once their version is recorded in `schema_migrations`, so this change will not “drop and recreate the top_topics table” on operators who already ran it during normal `db:migrate`. The finding’s claimed automatic data loss on the “next schema operation” is not supported by what’s shown in the diff (it would only matter if someone explicitly re-ran/rolled back that migration or rebuilt the DB).

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The Disqus import task silently drops the `--category` option and the original `created_at` timestamps, rerouting through TopicEmbed.import_remote instead of PostCreator — a behavior change to an existing tool that is not traceable to the embedding requirement. Anyone running the documented `disqus import -c <category>` invocation now gets a hard Thor error (unknown option) with no replacement, and imported posts lose their original creation dates; the user is bitten on the next import run.

adjudication.rationale: The diff removes the Thor option `method_option :category` from `lib/tasks/disqus.thor`, so any existing invocation using `-c/--category` will now fail with an unknown option error. It also replaces `PostCreator.new(... created_at: Date.parse(t[:created_at]), category: category_id)` with `TopicEmbed.import_remote(user, t[:link], title: t[:title])`, and `TopicEmbed.import_remote`/`TopicEmbed.import` do not pass `created_at` (or category) into `PostCreator`, so imported topics/posts will no longer preserve original timestamps and will use default/current timestamps instead. This is a breaking behavior change introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] `i.content.scrub` crashes with NoMethodError when a feed item has no content element (common for RSS 2.0 feeds or Atom entries with only a summary). The hourly PollFeed job raises mid-loop, aborting import of all remaining items; with retry: false the whole feed import silently stops at the first malformed item until manual intervention.

adjudication.rationale: In `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb`, the loop does `content = CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)`. If a feed item lacks a `content` field (e.g., only `summary`/`description`), `i.content` can be `nil`, making `nil.scrub` raise `NoMethodError` and abort the job mid-iteration. Since the job sets `sidekiq_options retry: false`, this exception would stop further imports until the next scheduled run (and repeatedly fail on the same item if the feed stays unchanged).

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The raw_html cook path returns `raw` before `Plugin::Filter.apply(:after_post_cook, ...)`, so plugins registered on that filter are silently bypassed for imported posts — a core pipeline behavioral fork introduced solely to serve embedding. Site operators relying on plugins that hook after_post_cook (e.g. link rewriting, media transformations) get inconsistent behavior: every RSS-imported post skips those transforms with no setting to control it.

adjudication.rationale: In `app/models/post.rb`, `cook` now returns `raw` early when `cook_method == Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`, which occurs before `Plugin::Filter.apply(:after_post_cook, ...)`. In `app/models/topic_embed.rb`, imported RSS/remote posts are created with `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` via `PostCreator`, so those imported posts will skip the `:after_post_cook` plugin hook entirely, creating inconsistent behavior for plugins that rely on that filter.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The resize postMessage is sent to `request.referer` as targetOrigin, coupling the embed layout to a header that is only guaranteed present because of the controller filter — and embed.js checks `discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin)` with no trailing-slash handling on either side. Any deployment where SiteSetting base_url has a trailing slash or the browser suppresses Referer (privacy settings, meta referrer) breaks iframe auto-resize, leaving the embed iframe stuck at default height; users see clipped comments.

adjudication.rationale: In `app/views/layouts/embed.html.erb`, the iframe calls `parent.postMessage(..., '<%= request.referer %>')`. `request.referer` is typically a full URL including path/query, but `postMessage`’s `targetOrigin` must be `*` or an origin (scheme+host+port), not a full URL; this can prevent the resize message from being sent/delivered, breaking auto-resize. The diff also shows embed.js depends on receiving that message to set `iframe.height`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] `response.headers['X-Frame-Options'] = "ALLOWALL"` is placed after the raising referer check and inside a method whose rescue re-raises, so the header-setting line is dead code on every rejection path. Maintainers reading the filter conclude the header is always applied; the successful path works only by accident of ordering, and any refactor that reorders the lines will silently drop the clickjacking relaxation the embed depends on.

adjudication.rationale: In `EmbedController#ensure_embeddable`, the `X-Frame-Options = "ALLOWALL"` header is only meant to be set on the success path (after the host/referer checks pass). It is not “dead code” generally: it runs whenever both `SiteSetting.embeddable_host` is present and `URI(request.referer || '').host` matches. It’s true it won’t run on rejection paths, but those paths raise `Discourse::InvalidAccess` and abort the request anyway, so the finding’s implication that the clickjacking relaxation is applied “only by accident” or that the line is dead code is a misread of the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] PollFeed crashes with NoMethodError when a feed item has no content element (plain RSS 2.0 feeds expose description, not content/content:encoded), because i.content is nil and nil.scrub raises. Any RSS (non-Atom) feed whose items lack content:encoded kills the entire poll job on the first item; every subsequent item in that feed is never imported and the scheduled job fails hourly with no partial progress.

If a feed item lacks a `content` field (common in RSS 2.0 where `description` is used instead of `content:encoded`), `i.content` will be `nil` and calling `nil.scrub` will raise `NoMethodError`, aborting the entire poll loop/job.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] TopicEmbed.import's update path does `post = embed.post; PostRevisor.new(post)` with no nil check, so an embed whose post was deleted crashes, and since import is called in a loop over all feed items, one bad embed aborts the whole poll. A single topic/post deleted by a moderator (posts can be deleted while topic_embeds rows persist — there is no dependent destroy or FK) makes Jobs::PollFeed raise mid-loop, permanently poisoning all feed imports for every item after that one.

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicEmbed.import`, the update path does `post = embed.post` and then unconditionally constructs `PostRevisor.new(post)` when the content hash changes (app/models/topic_embed.rb). Because `topic_embeds.post_id` has no FK in the migration and there is no dependent-destroy shown, an embed row can remain while the referenced `Post` is deleted; in that case `embed.post` will be `nil` and `PostRevisor.new(nil)` will raise. `Jobs::PollFeed#poll_feed` calls `TopicEmbed.import` inside `rss.items.each` with no rescue (app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb), so one such exception would abort the loop/job and prevent processing subsequent feed items.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The loading view reloads unconditionally every 30 seconds forever, even when the RetrieveTopic job can never succeed (e.g. embed_by_username unset so fetch_http returns early, or the embed_url host check fails after enqueue). Every visitor to a page whose article can never be imported drives an infinite reload loop in their browser, each cycle hitting /embed/best and enqueueing another RetrieveTopic job (throttled only per-URL for 60s), producing permanent background job churn and a never-loading embed.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `app/views/embed/loading.html.erb` with a `setTimeout(document.location.reload, 30000)` that always reloads (no stop condition). In `EmbedController#best`, when `TopicEmbed.topic_id_for_embed(embed_url)` is nil it always enqueues `Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, ..., embed_url: embed_url)` and renders `loading`. However `TopicRetriever#retrieve` can permanently no-op (e.g. `invalid_host?` returns true when `SiteSetting.embeddable_host != URI(@embed_url).host`, or `fetch_http` returns early when `embed_by_username` is unset / user missing). In those cases the embed will never become available, yet clients will keep reloading and triggering `/embed/best`, repeatedly enqueueing `RetrieveTopic` jobs (and in the `invalid_host?` case even bypassing the redis throttle due to short-circuiting), causing a never-loading embed and ongoing job churn.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] feed_key computes a SHA1-based 'feed-modified' cache key but nothing in the diff ever reads or writes it, so the intended conditional-fetch/last-poll dedupe was never wired up. Every hourly poll re-opens and fully parses the feed and runs TopicEmbed.where(embed_url:).first plus a SHA1 comparison for every historical item — a 5-year blog with thousands of items does thousands of pointless DB lookups per poll forever, and the dead method misleads the next maintainer into thinking caching exists.

adjudication.rationale: In `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb`, the method `feed_key` computes a Redis-style key (`"feed-modified:#{Digest::SHA1.hexdigest(...)}`) but nothing in the diff ever calls `feed_key` or uses it to store/read a last-modified/etag/last-poll value. The implemented `poll_feed` always does `SimpleRSS.parse open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` and iterates `rss.items` on every run, calling `TopicEmbed.import` for each item, which performs at least `TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: url).first` per item and computes `content_sha1`. This is a real, diff-grounded scalability/efficiency concern and a misleading dead method, but it doesn't make the feature incorrect/broken by itself.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] perform_retrieve synchronously invokes Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({}) inline — a full-site feed fetch, parse, and per-item import — inside the single-URL retrieve job, coupling one embed request to the entire feed pipeline. A visitor embedding one new article blocks a Sidekiq worker for the duration of downloading and importing the whole feed; with the no_throttle staff bypass, concurrent embed views each trigger full feed polls, multiplying load and serializing behind a single global feed_polling_url setting that the data model can't extend to multiple feeds.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `TopicRetriever#perform_retrieve` calling `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})` inline when `SiteSetting.feed_polling_enabled?` is true, rather than enqueuing it (`lib/topic_retriever.rb`, `perform_retrieve`). `Jobs::PollFeed#poll_feed` performs a synchronous network fetch (`SimpleRSS.parse open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)`) and iterates/imports all items (`rss.items.each ... TopicEmbed.import`), so a single embed retrieval can be coupled to a full feed poll and block the worker/request path. This is a concrete design/performance coupling introduced by the change, not a correctness defect per se.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The raw_html cook_method early-returns before Plugin::Filter.apply(:after_post_cook, ...), so one category of posts silently bypasses the plugin cooking contract that all other posts pass through. Any site relying on an after_post_cook plugin filter (e.g. Onebox rewriting, link normalization, profanity filtering) gets none of it on imported feed posts, and a plugin author debugging 'works for user posts but not imported posts' has no indication the branch was skipped.

adjudication.rationale: In `app/models/post.rb`, `cook` now early-returns `raw` when `cook_method == Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`, which bypasses `Plugin::Filter.apply(:after_post_cook, ...)` entirely. The diff also introduces `cook_method: :raw_html` for imported content in `TopicEmbed.import` via `PostCreator`. This is a real, diff-grounded behavioral divergence that can surprise plugins relying on `:after_post_cook`, but it’s not unambiguously a correctness defect since skipping the cooking pipeline for “raw HTML” appears intentional.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] topic_id and post_id are plain integer columns with no foreign keys or indexes, so nothing prevents a topic_embed row pointing at a deleted/nonexistent topic or post, and topic-side lookups (given a topic, find its embed) require a full scan. Deleting a topic or post leaves an orphaned topic_embeds row; the next import for that URL takes the update path and crashes (see separate finding), and any future admin query 'which embed belongs to topic X' has no index to use.

adjudication.rationale: In db/migrate/20131217174004_create_topic_embeds.rb, topic_embeds defines topic_id and post_id as plain integer columns and only adds a unique index on embed_url. There are no foreign keys and no indexes on topic_id/post_id, so referential integrity isn’t enforced and queries like TopicEmbed.where(topic_id: ...) (seen in spec/models/topic_embed_spec.rb) would not be indexed. The orphan/crash scenario on delete is plausible (embed.post could become nil in TopicEmbed.import’s update path), but deletions/orphan creation aren’t shown directly in this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The disqus import thor task silently drops the documented `:category` / `-c` option, so all imported topics now land in uncategorized regardless of the operator's command line. Operators running `thor disqus:import -c mycategory` after this deploy get every imported thread in the wrong (uncategorized) category with no error — the option is simply ignored; the diff gives no human-accepted rationale for removing the capability.

adjudication.rationale: In `lib/tasks/disqus.thor`, the `method_option :category, aliases: '-c'` is removed and the associated `category_id` lookup/passing into `PostCreator` is deleted. The task now calls `TopicEmbed.import_remote(user, t[:link], title: t[:title])`, which (per diff) ultimately uses `PostCreator.new(user, ...)` without any `category` option, so imported topics can no longer be assigned to an operator-specified category and will fall back to the default category behavior (likely uncategorized). The finding’s “silently ignored” detail isn’t directly verifiable from the diff (Thor may error on unknown options), but the loss of `-c` functionality is clearly introduced here.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] An already-shipped, unrelated migration (`CreateTopTopics`) is edited in this PR to add `force: true`, which drops and recreates the table on databases that already ran it or rebuild from scratch mid-PR. Any environment where this migration runs again (db:reset-adjacent workflows, fresh clones interleaved with the change) silently destroys top_topics data; this is scope creep into an unrelated migration with no accepted justification in the PR's stated intent.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does modify an existing, unrelated migration: `db/migrate/20131223171005_create_top_topics.rb` changes `create_table :top_topics` to `create_table :top_topics, force: true`. In Rails, `force: true` will drop the table if it exists when that migration is executed, so rerunning/redoing that migration could wipe `top_topics` data. However, on a typical already-migrated environment this migration won’t run again just because the file changed, so the finding’s claim that it will drop data on databases that already ran it is overstated. The real, diff-grounded issue is the risky scope creep of editing an old migration and introducing table-drop behavior if the migration is re-executed in certain workflows (redo/rollback/replay).

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The `raw_html` cook path returns `raw` before `Plugin::Filter.apply(:after_post_cook, ...)` runs, so posts imported via embeds silently bypass every registered after_post_cook plugin hook. Sites relying on plugins that mutate cooked output (onebox rewriting, affiliate stripping, custom sanitization) get unsanitized, unfiltered HTML in embed-imported posts rendered with `raw post.cooked` in embed views; plugin authors and admins have no signal that the hook contract no longer holds for these posts.

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `Post#cook` to `return raw if cook_method == Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`, which definitively skips `Plugin::Filter.apply(:after_post_cook, ...)` for those posts. The embed import path (`TopicEmbed.import` via `PostCreator` with `cook_method: :raw_html`) then renders with `<%= raw post.cooked %>` in `app/views/embed/best.html.erb`, so any plugins relying on `:after_post_cook` to mutate/sanitize cooked output will not run for embed-imported posts. This is a concrete behavior break introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The revisor's save behavior is globally changed from unconditional `@post.save` to `@post.save(validate: !@opts[:skip_validations])`, altering the validation contract for every existing caller of revise!, not just the embed importer that needed it. Any existing code path that calls revise! with user-controlled opts can now persist invalid posts whenever skip_validations leaks in, and future revisor callers inherit an easy validation-bypass footgun — a core-object semantic change hidden inside a feature PR about embedding.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does globally change PostRevisor’s persistence semantics: in `lib/post_revisor.rb#update_post` it replaces unconditional `@post.save` with `@post.save(validate: !@opts[:skip_validations])`. This enables validation bypass for any `revise!` caller that supplies `skip_validations`, and the new embed importer does exactly that (`TopicEmbed.import` calls `revisor.revise!(..., skip_validations: true, ...)`). While the diff doesn’t show any *existing* callers passing user-controlled opts, the concern about introducing a broad validation-bypass knob into a core revisor is diff-grounded and scope/contract related rather than a directly provable defect here.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] TopicEmbed.import stores externally-fetched content as raw HTML with no sanitization, and the embed view renders it with `raw post.cooked`, enabling stored XSS. The feed-polling path passes CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content) straight into PostCreator with cook_method raw_html, which makes Post#cook return the raw string verbatim (app/models/post.rb `return raw if cook_method == Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`), and app/views/embed/best.html.erb renders `<%= raw post.cooked %>` — so any <script>, inline event handler, or javascript: link in the RSS/Atom item content executes in every visitor's browser on the embedding site. If the polled feed (or a MITM on the plain-http feed URL) is compromised, the attacker runs script in the Discourse origin and the embeddable host.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces a `raw_html` cook method that makes `Post#cook` return the post’s `raw` verbatim (`return raw if cook_method == Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` in app/models/post.rb). `TopicEmbed.import` creates posts with `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` and `skip_validations: true` (app/models/topic_embed.rb), and the feed polling job passes `CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)` from an external RSS/Atom feed directly into `TopicEmbed.import` (app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb) without any sanitization. The embed view then renders the content as HTML via `<%= raw post.cooked %>` (app/views/embed/best.html.erb). Together, this is a verifiable stored-XSS path for externally-fetched content.

adjudication_records.issue_text:
[BUG] The imported-from footer interpolates the URL directly into an HTML attribute without escaping: `contents << "
#{I18n.t('embed.imported_from', link: "#{url}")} "`. The only URL validation is the prefix regex /^https?:///, so an embed_url or RSS item link like `http://eviltrout.com/x' onmouseover=alert(1) b='` (host matches embeddable_host, satisfying TopicRetriever#invalid_host?) breaks out of the href attribute; since the post is cooked as raw_html and rendered with `raw`, this is stored XSS in the Discourse embed page triggered by any user who requests /embed/best with that embed_url.

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicEmbed.import`, the code appends an HTML snippet that interpolates `url` directly into a single-quoted `href` attribute: `"#{url}"`. The only validation shown is `return unless url =~ /^https?\:\/\//`, which does not prevent quotes or other attribute-breaking characters in the URL. The imported post is created with `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`, and `Post#cook` returns `raw` for `:raw_html`, so no sanitization/rendering pipeline runs. The embed view then renders `raw post.cooked`, making this a stored-XSS vector if an attacker can cause an embedded/retrieved URL like `http://eviltrout.com/x' onmouseover='...'` (same host) to be imported.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The postMessage origin check uses substring containment (`discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1`) instead of exact origin equality, so any origin whose string contains the Discourse URL passes. A malicious page at https://eviltrout.com.attacker.com (or any URL embedding the discourse base URL as a substring) passes the check and can drive the iframe via cross-origin messages; currently the only effect is setting iframe height, but the guard is a broken security boundary that later message types will inherit.
matched_golden_ids: The current origin validation using indexOf is insufficient and can be bypassed. An attacker could use a malicious domain like evil-discourseUrl.com to pass this check.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both point out that using `indexOf`/substring checks for validating `postMessage` origins is insecure and can be bypassed by malicious domains that include the trusted URL as a substring (e.g., `evil-discourseUrl.com`). The candidate describes the same underlying origin-validation flaw and bypass scenario.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The SSRF host check (invalid_host?) is enforced once before the fetch, but open-uri transparently follows HTTP redirects, so the embeddable_host check does not constrain where the actual request lands. The embeddable host (or anything that can make it issue a 302) can redirect open(url) to http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/ or an internal service; the retrieved body is then run through Readability and stored/rendered as raw HTML, letting the operator of the configured host exfiltrate internal-network responses through the Discourse embed.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `TopicRetriever#invalid_host?` which only checks `URI(@embed_url).host` against `SiteSetting.embeddable_host`, but the actual fetch happens later in `TopicEmbed.import_remote` via `open(url).read` (open-uri). Since open-uri follows HTTP redirects, an allowed embeddable host can 30x-redirect the request to an internal/metadata URL, bypassing the initial host allowlist. The retrieved body is then persisted (`TopicEmbed.import`) and rendered back out (posts imported with `cook_method: raw_html`, and `embed/best.html.erb` uses `<%= raw post.cooked %>`), enabling SSRF-to-exfiltration. This is directly grounded in `TopicRetriever#fetch_http` -> `TopicEmbed.import_remote` using `open(url)` with no redirect/endpoint revalidation.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] ensure_embeddable gates the endpoint on the Referer header, which is client-controlled and trivially spoofed by any non-browser or headless client, so the referer-host check provides no real access control. Any attacker can curl /embed/best?embed_url=... with a forged Referer to bypass the host gate; impact is currently limited to triggering RetrieveTopic jobs (throttled to once/60s per URL per non-staff user) and viewing public topic content, but the control is security theater and downstream code treats it as an authorization decision.

adjudication.rationale: `EmbedController#ensure_embeddable` treats `request.referer` as an authorization gate (`URI(request.referer || '').host != SiteSetting.embeddable_host` raises `Discourse::InvalidAccess`). The Referer header is client-controlled and can be trivially forged by non-browser clients, so this check does not actually prevent direct access to `GET /embed/best?embed_url=...` (an attacker can supply a matching Referer). While `TopicRetriever#invalid_host?` later constrains retrieval to `SiteSetting.embeddable_host`, the controller’s referer-host gate is still ineffective as access control and the code clearly relies on it to decide whether the endpoint is allowed.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The three guard tests are tautological: each stubs only one SiteSetting while the other two already default to disabled/blank, so every test passes even if the corresponding guard in Jobs::PollFeed#execute is deleted. Deleting `SiteSetting.feed_polling_enabled? &&` (or either other condition) from execute leaves the suite green; the guard logic that prevents the job from polling an unconfigured feed is verified by nothing. The author's counter-argument is 'stubs isolate each condition' — but they don't: the unstubbed settings' defaults already make poll_feed unreachable, so the tests never discriminate a present guard from an absent one.

adjudication.rationale: In spec/jobs/poll_feed_spec.rb the three “requires …” tests each stub only one SiteSetting to a failing value, but the other two settings default to false/blank per config/site_settings.yml (feed_polling_enabled: false, feed_polling_url: '', embed_by_username: ''). That means poll_feed is unreachable regardless, so those tests would still pass even if the corresponding condition in Jobs::PollFeed#execute were removed. The “delegates to poll_feed” test stubs all three to truthy, so it also wouldn’t fail if any single guard were deleted. This is a concrete, diff-grounded test gap, not a runtime defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The first two tests assert only `response.should_not be_success`, which is satisfied by any failure mode, including the before_filter's Discourse::InvalidAccess from the blank default embeddable_host rather than the param-missing / host-missing behavior they claim to test. The 'is 404 without an embed_url' test would pass identically if `params.require(:embed_url)` were removed and the action returned 200 with a nil embed_url — the actual contract (400/404 for missing param vs 403 for host errors) is never distinguished, so a regression to a wrong status code or wrong error path ships undetected.

adjudication.rationale: In `spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb`, the first two examples only assert `response.should_not be_success` (`"is 404 without an embed_url"` and `"raises an error with a missing host"`). Given the controller’s `before_filter :ensure_embeddable` (in `app/controllers/embed_controller.rb`) raises `Discourse::InvalidAccess` when `SiteSetting.embeddable_host.blank?` or when referer/host checks fail, these specs can pass due to the before_filter failure path rather than specifically exercising `params.require(:embed_url)` or distinguishing missing-param vs missing-host error contracts. This is a test-specific gap/ambiguity introduced with the new controller and specs, not a functional defect in the runtime behavior shown in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The success-context tests exercise only mocks: `TopicView.expects(:new)` returns nil (so the template renders against a nil @topic_view), `TopicRetriever.expects` replaces the retrieval, and the only real-behavior assertion lives in a shared `after` block, so neither test verifies rendered output, the enqueued job's arguments (user_id, embed_url), or the render of 'loading'. If EmbedController#best stopped enqueuing :retrieve_topic with the right embed_url, or rendered the wrong template, or TopicView were constructed with wrong options, these tests still pass as long as a mock was poked; the mocha stub for TopicView.new returning nil means the view layer is never genuinely exercised and any template crash is masked by the assertion-free it-block body.

adjudication.rationale: In `spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb` the “success” examples largely assert that certain collaborators are called (e.g., `TopicEmbed.expects(:topic_id_for_embed)`, `TopicView.expects(:new)`) and otherwise only check `response` success/X-Frame-Options in a shared `after`. They do not assert which template is rendered (e.g., `'loading'` when no `topic_id`), nor do they assert that `Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, user_id: ..., embed_url: ...)` was invoked with the right args (the controller code in `EmbedController#best` enqueues this job). This is a concrete, diff-grounded test coverage gap around the controller’s new behavior, even though parts of the finding overstate view rendering details.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The 'valid host' tests stub `retrieved_recently?` and mock `perform_retrieve`, so TopicRetriever's actual Redis throttle ($redis.setnx/expire 60s) and perform_retrieve's dedup/feed-polling/fetch_http branches are never executed by any test in the diff. A broken retrieved_recently? (e.g. setnx key typo, missing expire leaking keys forever, or the throttle never firing so every embed request re-fetches the remote site) passes this suite unchanged; the tests only verify that a mocked method is called when another mocked method returns false — a tautology against the real code.

adjudication.rationale: In spec/components/topic_retriever_spec.rb, the “valid host” examples stub `retrieved_recently?` to true/false and only assert whether `perform_retrieve` is called. That means the real Redis throttle in `retrieved_recently?` (the `$redis.setnx`/`expire` logic in lib/topic_retriever.rb) is never executed by any test in this diff, and `perform_retrieve`’s internal branches (dedup `TopicEmbed.exists?`, optional `Jobs::PollFeed`, and `fetch_http`) are also not exercised. adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The 'Supports updating the post' test checks only that the new content appears, never that exactly one TopicEmbed/topic still exists (no duplicate topic created on re-import) nor that content_sha1 was updated. The update path's main risk — re-import creating a second topic because the embed lookup or content_sha1 comparison regressed — would still satisfy the regex assertion; a future change breaking the `embed.blank?` branch silently doubles topics per feed poll, and this spec stays green.

adjudication.rationale: In `spec/models/topic_embed_spec.rb`, the "Supports updating the post" example only asserts `post.cooked` matches `/new contents/` after a second `TopicEmbed.import(...)` call with the same URL. It does not assert that the existing `TopicEmbed` row was reused (e.g., `TopicEmbed.count` unchanged / same `topic_id` / same `post_id`) nor that `content_sha1` was updated via `embed.update_column(:content_sha1, content_sha1)` in the update path of `TopicEmbed.import`. adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The only positive test asserts `poll_feed` is invoked once and nothing else, so PollFeed#poll_feed's entire body — feed parsing, `i.link`/`i.id` fallback, CGI.unescapeHTML, content scrub, and the TopicEmbed.import call per item — has zero coverage in this diff. A crash in poll_feed (e.g. `i.content` nil raising on .scrub, or open() raising on a bad feed URL) reaches production the first time an admin enables feed polling, because every spec stops at the delegation boundary; with `retry: false` in sidekiq_options the job fails permanently with no diagnostics.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds substantial new logic in `Jobs::PollFeed#poll_feed` (open-uri fetch + `SimpleRSS.parse`, per-item URL fallback `i.link`/`i.id`, `CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)`, and `TopicEmbed.import` calls), but the only new spec (`spec/jobs/poll_feed_spec.rb`) exercises only `execute`’s gating and that it delegates to `poll_feed`, without asserting any behavior of `poll_feed` itself. The additional notes about specific crashes/production impact are plausible but not directly verifiable from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] No test in the diff exercises TopicRetriever#perform_retrieve, #fetch_http, or TopicEmbed.import_remote, and no spec file references them (checked spec/components/topic_retriever_spec.rb, spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb, spec/models/topic_embed_spec.rb, spec/jobs/poll_feed_spec.rb — all mock or bypass these methods). The invalid_host? rescue-branch ordering, the feed_polling shortcut, and the embed_by_username user lookup in fetch_http are the live code paths serving every embed request, yet a typo in any of them ships undetected; the retriever spec's guard tests pass against a TopicRetriever whose retrieve body is `nil`.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds nontrivial runtime logic in `TopicRetriever` (`perform_retrieve`, `fetch_http`, RSS shortcut via `Jobs::PollFeed`, and `embed_by_username` lookup) and `TopicEmbed.import_remote` (Readability/open-uri path), but the added specs do not execute these code paths. `spec/components/topic_retriever_spec.rb` explicitly mocks `perform_retrieve` and stubs `retrieved_recently?`, so it only tests guard behavior in `retrieve` and would not catch regressions/typos inside `perform_retrieve`/`fetch_http`. `spec/models/topic_embed_spec.rb` covers `.import` but not `.import_remote`. adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] force: true is added to the already-shipped CreateTopTopics migration, making it destructive on re-run. Any environment that re-runs this migration (db:migrate:redo, restored schema_migrations, or a re-cloned setup importing a dump with the table populated) silently DROPs the existing top_topics table and destroys all its data before recreating it empty; the lens's exact 'shipped migration made destructive on re-run' failure.

adjudication.rationale: The diff modifies an existing migration `db/migrate/20131223171005_create_top_topics.rb` by changing `create_table :top_topics do |t|` to `create_table :top_topics, force: true do |t|`.
