adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] create_table :topic_embeds uses force: true, so any pre-existing topic_embeds table (e.g. left by a failed first run or a parallel deploy) is silently dropped with all its embed mappings. An operator re-running the migration after a partial/failed application loses the topic_id/post_id/embed_url associations, orphaning imported topics from their source URLs and causing duplicate topics on the next feed poll.

adjudication.rationale: The new migration `db/migrate/20131217174004_create_topic_embeds.rb` uses `create_table :topic_embeds, force: true`, which instructs Rails to drop and recreate the table if it already exists. In a rerun/partial-failure/parallel deploy scenario where `topic_embeds` exists but the migration is executed again, this would silently delete existing embed mappings (`topic_id`, `post_id`, `embed_url`, `content_sha1`), matching the finding's data-loss and duplicate-import risk.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The Disqus import path switched from PostCreator with created_at: Date.parse(t[:created_at]) to TopicEmbed.import_remote, which drops the original creation date entirely. Anyone importing a Disqus export after this change gets topics dated 'now' instead of their historical dates — a field-fidelity loss on migration data; the created_at plumbing exists in PostCreator but is never passed by the new code path.

adjudication.rationale: In `lib/tasks/disqus.thor`, the import path changed from `PostCreator.new(... created_at: Date.parse(t[:created_at]) ...)` to `TopicEmbed.import_remote(user, t[:link], title: t[:title])`. `TopicEmbed.import_remote`/`TopicEmbed.import` ultimately call `PostCreator.new(...)` without any `created_at` option, so imported topics/posts will get the current timestamp instead of the Disqus thread’s original `t[:created_at]`. The diff also shows `PostCreator` still supports `created_at` via `setup_post`, but the new code path never passes it.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] TopicEmbed.import update path uses PostRevisor#revise! but never updates the topic title when the feed title changes, and a revisor failure leaves content_sha1 unchanged only because update_column runs after — but if revise! raises (invalid content), the rescue is absent and the scheduled job (retry: false) permanently skips that item. Feed items whose revision raises lose their update forever (PollFeed has sidekiq_options retry: false, so the exception kills the entire poll run mid-list and subsequent items are never processed until the next hour's partial re-run hits the same item again).

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicEmbed.import`, the update path only revises the post raw (`PostRevisor#revise!` with new raw HTML) and updates `content_sha1`, but never updates the topic/post title when the feed item's `title` changes (only the create path uses `PostCreator.new(... title: title ...)`). Also, `Jobs::PollFeed` iterates `rss.items.each` without per-item error handling and sets `sidekiq_options retry: false`, so any exception inside `TopicEmbed.import` (e.g., from revising/parsing/open-uri) would abort the whole polling run and skip later items until the next schedule. The finding’s “revise! raises (invalid content)” and “lose their update forever” parts are somewhat speculative, but the lack of title update and lack of rescue + retry:false behavior are directly supported by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The rss.items loop has no per-item or per-feed error handling, so a single malformed item aborts the entire poll mid-loop with no log and no error surfaced. If any item's i.content is nil (valid in RSS/Atom) `i.content.scrub` raises NoMethodError, or if any item's link/id resolution fails, the job dies after importing a prefix of the feed: the remaining items are silently skipped while the already-imported ones look successful, and sidekiq_options retry: false means nothing retries or reports until the next hourly run, which fails the same way — a persistent silent partial import.

adjudication.rationale: In the newly added `Jobs::PollFeed#poll_feed`, the code iterates `rss.items.each` and unconditionally does `content = CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)` (and then `TopicEmbed.import(...)`) with no per-item rescue/logging. If any item has `i.content == nil`, this will raise `NoMethodError` on `scrub`, aborting the job mid-loop after partially importing earlier items. Additionally, `sidekiq_options retry: false` means the failure won’t be retried and will persistently fail on the same bad item until the next scheduled run.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] SimpleRSS.parse open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url) performs an outbound HTTP fetch with no timeout. A slow or hung feed host blocks the Sidekiq worker thread indefinitely; with retry: false the poll is not retried, and because TopicRetriever#perform_retrieve invokes this same poll synchronously inside a RetrieveTopic job, one hung feed also wedges the embed-retrieval job and the user's iframe stays on the loading page with no timeout ever firing.

adjudication.rationale: In `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb`, `SimpleRSS.parse open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` performs an outbound fetch via `open-uri` without specifying any `open_timeout`/`read_timeout`, so a slow/hung feed can block the Sidekiq thread indefinitely. This is amplified because the job sets `sidekiq_options retry: false`, and `lib/topic_retriever.rb` calls `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})` synchronously inside `TopicRetriever#perform_retrieve`, which is invoked from `Jobs::RetrieveTopic`—so one hung feed can wedge embed retrieval as described.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] TopicEmbed.import_remote calls open(url).read with no timeout and no size cap on the download. A request to /embed/best for a page whose host accepts the connection but stalls leaves the RetrieveTopic worker blocked forever on a socket read; the controller meanwhile rendered 'loading' and reported success (200), so the embed is never created and the end user reloads into the same loop indefinitely.

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicEmbed.import_remote`, the code does `Readability::Document.new(open(url).read, ...)` with no explicit timeouts or response size limits. This method is invoked by `TopicRetriever#fetch_http` during `Jobs::RetrieveTopic` execution, so a slow/stalling remote host can block a Sidekiq worker on the network read. Meanwhile `EmbedController#best` enqueues the job and `render 'loading'` (default 200), and `loading.html.erb` auto-reloads every 30s, so if the job is stuck the embed can remain uncreated and the client can loop indefinitely. The lack of timeouts/limits is directly visible in the diff; the “forever” aspect depends on runtime defaults but the unbounded blocking risk is real.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The update path assumes embed.post is non-nil, but TopicEmbed has no dependency on the post surviving; PostRevisor.new(post).revise! crashes when the referenced post was deleted. When a feed re-import hits an embed whose post was deleted (post_id null: false does not prevent the post row itself being removed), PostRevisor.new(nil) raises NoMethodError inside the scheduled poll, aborting the remaining feed items with no recovery and no log of which URL was at fault.

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicEmbed.import`, the update path does `post = embed.post` and then unconditionally calls `PostRevisor.new(post).revise!(...)` when the SHA changes (app/models/topic_embed.rb). If the associated Post row was deleted, `embed.post` will be `nil` (no FK constraint is added; `post_id null: false` only prevents NULL, not dangling references). That would cause `PostRevisor` to be initialized with `nil` and likely raise, which would abort `Jobs::PollFeed#poll_feed` mid-iteration since it has no rescue (app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb).

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] TopicView.new(topic_id, ...) raises when the topic_embed row points at a deleted or otherwise unviewable topic, producing a raw 500 in the embed iframe. Once an embed's topic is deleted (or made restricted for anonymous viewers), every /embed/best request for that URL returns a 500 error page inside the publisher's iframe instead of a 4xx or the loading/fallback view, permanently breaking comments on that article.

adjudication.rationale: In EmbedController#best, if TopicEmbed.topic_id_for_embed(embed_url) returns an id, the code unconditionally calls `TopicView.new(topic_id, current_user, {best: 5})` with no validation that the topic still exists or is viewable (and no rescue/fallback). Since `topic_id_for_embed` is just `TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: ...).pluck(:topic_id).first`, a stale embed row can return a deleted/missing topic_id, or an unviewable topic for the current_user, and any exception from TopicView construction would bubble up and render an error in the iframe rather than `loading`/a 4xx.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The retrieve is fire-and-forget: the controller enqueues RetrieveTopic and renders 'loading' with no path for the job's failure to ever reach the user. If the retrieval job fails (unreachable article, readability returning no content, or the throttle/redis path erroring), the iframe reloads every 30 seconds forever showing 'Loading Discussion...' — the site owner gets no error signal, and each reload enqueues another job that silently no-ops, so the failure is invisible on both the user page and Discourse's own UI.

adjudication.rationale: In `EmbedController#best`, when no `topic_id` exists it unconditionally `Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, ...)` and renders `loading`. The `loading.html.erb` then `document.location.reload()` every 30s, which will re-hit `best` and enqueue again as long as `TopicEmbed.topic_id_for_embed(embed_url)` remains nil. There is no error state or backoff path in the controller/view, and the job path can silently no-op (`TopicRetriever#retrieve` returns without `perform_retrieve` if `invalid_host?` or `retrieved_recently?`), or fail (e.g., network/open-uri/readability/redis exceptions) without any user-visible signal. This creates an indefinite “Loading Discussion...” loop with repeated enqueues on persistent failure.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] perform_retrieve invokes the full hourly feed poll (Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})) synchronously and inline inside the RetrieveTopic job. Every embed miss pays the cost of fetching and re-importing the entire RSS feed inline — combined with the missing timeout above, a large or slow feed multiplies worker occupancy, and the scheduled hourly poll plus these inline polls can run concurrently against the same feed with no lock, double-importing or racing on TopicEmbed.create! (unique index then raises ActiveRecord::RecordNotUnique aborting the job).

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicRetriever#perform_retrieve`, on an embed miss it synchronously calls `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})` when `SiteSetting.feed_polling_enabled?` is true. `Jobs::PollFeed#poll_feed` fetches and parses the entire feed inline via `open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` and iterates all items, so every miss can block the `RetrieveTopic` worker on network + full-feed work. There is also no locking/coordination: the scheduled `Jobs::PollFeed` (hourly) and multiple inline polls can run concurrently, and `TopicEmbed.import` does a read-then-`create!` against a unique index on `topic_embeds.embed_url`, so races can raise `ActiveRecord::RecordNotUnique` and abort the job.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] feed_key (the 'feed-modified:<sha1>' cache key) is computed but never read or written — the conditional-fetch caching it implies was never wired up. Every hourly poll and every inline poll from TopicRetriever fully re-downloads and re-processes the entire feed regardless of whether it changed; a large feed costs full bandwidth and full TopicEmbed.import reconciliation work each cycle, and the dead key misleads the next maintainer into believing modification-checking exists.

adjudication.rationale: In `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb`, `feed_key` computes a Redis-style key (`"feed-modified:<sha1>"`) but is never referenced from `execute` or `poll_feed` (or anywhere else in the diff). The actual polling logic always does `SimpleRSS.parse open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` and iterates `rss.items` every run, and `TopicRetriever#perform_retrieve` can also trigger `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})`, so there is no conditional-fetch / modification-check implemented despite the presence of `feed_key`. This is a real, diff-grounded maintainability/performance concern, not a functional correctness defect per se.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] TopicEmbed.import imposes no cap on the number of feed items processed or the size of content stored, and the feed loop iterates every item unconditionally. A feed (or an attacker-controlled embedded page, given the referer check only validates host) can supply arbitrarily many items or arbitrarily large article bodies, which are stored verbatim as raw_html posts — unbounded DB growth and job runtime per poll with no maximum to stop it.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces unbounded ingestion of external content: `Jobs::PollFeed#poll_feed` parses a remote feed and iterates `rss.items.each` with no limit on item count and passes `i.content` through to `TopicEmbed.import` (app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb). `TopicEmbed.import` stores the (absolutized) contents into a post with `cook_method: :raw_html` and `skip_validations: true` (app/models/topic_embed.rb), so large/ numerous items can directly translate into large DB writes and long runtime. Additionally, `TopicRetriever#perform_retrieve` can trigger `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})` during embed retrieval (lib/topic_retriever.rb), making this a realistic resource-exhaustion vector when a configured feed is large or attacker-controlled.
